name: Pierogi
description: Eastern European dumplings of unleavened dough, typically filled with a savory or sweet stuffing.

name: Empanada
description: A baked or fried turnover consisting of pastry and a savory filling, common in Southern European and Latin American cultures.

name: Wonton
description: A type of Chinese dumpling commonly found in soups or fried as an appetizer.

name: Dumpling
description: A broad class of dishes that consist of pieces of dough wrapped around a filling.

name: Samosa
description: A fried or baked pastry with a savory filling, such as spiced potatoes, onions, and peas.

name: Tamale
description: A Mesoamerican dish of seasoned filling wrapped in corn dough and steamed in a corn husk or banana leaf.

name: Ravioli
description: A type of pasta comprising a filling sealed between two layers of thin pasta dough.

name: Calzone
description: An Italian oven-baked folded pizza that originated in Naples.

name: Kefir
description: A fermented milk drink, similar to a thin yogurt, made from grains that are a symbiotic culture of bacteria and yeast.

name: Kombucha
description: A fermented, lightly effervescent, sweetened black or green tea drink.

name: Tempeh
description: A traditional Indonesian food made from fermented soybeans, formed into a cake.

name: Sauerkraut
description: Finely cut raw cabbage that has been fermented by various lactic acid bacteria.

name: Kimchi
description: A traditional Korean side dish of salted and fermented vegetables, such as napa cabbage and Korean radish.

name: Yogurt
description: A food produced by bacterial fermentation of milk.

name: Miso
description: A traditional Japanese seasoning produced by fermenting soybeans with salt and kōji.

name: Sourdough
description: Bread made by the fermentation of dough using naturally occurring lactobacilli and yeast.

name: Steak Tartare
description: A meat dish made from finely chopped or minced raw beef or horse meat.

name: Oysters
description: A common name for a number of different families of salt-water bivalve molluscs that are often eaten uncooked on the half shell.

name: Sashimi
description: A Japanese delicacy consisting of fresh raw fish or meat sliced into thin pieces and often eaten with soy sauce.

name: Carpaccio
description: A dish of meat or fish, thinly sliced or pounded thin, and served uncooked.

name: Crudo
description: An Italian and Spanish word for 'raw,' referring to dishes of uncooked fish or shellfish dressed with oil, citrus, and seasonings.

name: Kitfo
description: An Ethiopian dish of minced raw beef, marinated in a chili powder-based spice blend.

name: Ceviche
description: A South American dish of fresh raw fish cured in fresh citrus juices, most commonly lime or lemon.

name: Poke
description: A Hawaiian dish of diced raw fish, often served as an appetizer or a main course.

name: Anchovy
description: A small, common forage fish of the family Engraulidae, often salt-cured and used to add savory flavor.

name: Mushroom
description: The fleshy, spore-bearing fruiting body of a fungus, known for its deep, savory flavor.

name: Tomato Paste
description: A thick paste made by cooking tomatoes for several hours to reduce the water content, concentrating their flavor.

name: Nutritional Yeast
description: A deactivated yeast, sold as a food product with a cheesy, nutty, and savory flavor.

name: Parmesan
description: A hard, granular cheese, aged for at least 12 months, with a complex savory flavor.

name: Soy Sauce
description: A liquid condiment of Chinese origin, made from a fermented paste of soybeans, roasted grain, brine, and Aspergillus mold.

name: Fish Sauce
description: A liquid condiment made from fish or krill that have been coated in salt and fermented for up to two years.

name: Seaweed
description: Edible algae, such as nori or kombu, that are naturally high in glutamate and provide a savory flavor.

name: Baguette
description: A long, thin loaf of French bread that is commonly made from basic lean dough.

name: Beignet
description: A type of deep-fried pastry, typically made from choux pastry, popular in New Orleans.

name: Pretzel
description: A type of baked pastry made from dough that is commonly shaped into a knot.

name: Focaccia
description: A flat oven-baked Italian bread, similar in style and texture to pizza.

name: Pizza
description: A dish of Italian origin consisting of a usually round, flat base of leavened wheat-based dough topped with various ingredients.

name: Naan
description: A leavened, oven-baked flatbread found in the cuisines of West and South Asia.

name: Gnocchi
description: Small Italian dumplings made from potato, semolina, or flour, usually served with a sauce.

name: Pasta
description: A staple food of Italian cuisine, made from an unleavened dough of wheat flour mixed with water or eggs.

name: Harissa
description: A hot chili pepper paste, native to the Maghreb, made from roasted red peppers, spices, and herbs.

name: Sambal
description: A chili sauce or paste typically made from a mixture of chili peppers with secondary ingredients such as shrimp paste, garlic, and lime juice.

name: Sriracha
description: A type of hot sauce or chili sauce made from a paste of chili peppers, distilled vinegar, garlic, sugar, and salt.

name: Tabasco
description: A brand of hot sauce made from peppers, vinegar, and salt, aged in white oak barrels.

name: Gochujang
description: A savory, sweet, and spicy fermented condiment popular in Korean cooking.

name: Wasabi
description: A paste made from the rhizome of the Wasabia japonica plant, with an extremely strong pungency.

name: Horseradish
description: A root vegetable used as a spice and prepared as a condiment, known for its pungent taste and odor.

name: Mustard
description: A condiment made from whole, ground, or cracked seeds of its namesake plant, mixed with a liquid.

name: Goulash
description: A soup or stew of meat and vegetables seasoned with paprika and other spices, originating in Hungary.

name: Chili
description: A spicy stew containing chili peppers, meat (usually beef), and often tomatoes and beans.

name: Stew
description: A dish of solid food ingredients that have been cooked in liquid and served in the resultant gravy.

name: Cassoulet
description: A rich, slow-cooked casserole containing meat (typically pork sausages, goose, duck) and white beans, originating in southern France.

name: Ratatouille
description: A French Provençal stewed vegetable dish, originating in Nice.

name: Curry
description: A variety of dishes originating in the Indian subcontinent that use a complex combination of spices or herbs, usually including ground turmeric, cumin, and coriander.

name: Tagine
description: A North African stew of spiced meat and vegetables prepared by slow cooking in a shallow earthenware cooking dish with a tall, conical lid.

name: Paella
description: A Spanish rice dish originally from Valencia, cooked and served in a large shallow pan.

name: Prosciutto
description: An Italian dry-cured ham that is usually thinly sliced and served uncooked.

name: Salami
description: A type of cured sausage consisting of fermented and air-dried meat, typically beef or pork.

name: Bresaola
description: Air-dried, salted beef that has been aged two or three months until it becomes hard and turns a dark red, almost purple color.

name: Capicola
description: A traditional Italian and Corsican pork cold cut made from the dry-cured muscle running from the neck to the fourth or fifth rib of the pork shoulder.

name: Speck
description: An Italian cured, smoked meat native to the South Tyrol region, made from a boned pork leg.

name: Chorizo
description: A type of pork sausage originating from the Iberian Peninsula, often seasoned with smoked paprika.

name: Pancetta
description: An Italian salt-cured pork belly meat, similar to bacon but not smoked.

name: Bacon
description: A type of salt-cured pork prepared from several different cuts of meat, typically from the pork belly or from the less fatty back cuts.
